# fallfloor

> A reference build (a modelled company, not a real client) that runs a digital bank's everyday AI work — customer support, inbound message screening, a staff HR helpdesk — on WebLLM in the browsers of laptops it already owns, passed node to node over WebRTC with no server. Pre-registered thresholds, Ed25519-signed hash-linked receipts for every hop, grading against public labelled datasets, and a cost comparison against public cloud list prices with every source linked.

- Live page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/fallfloor/
- Source: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor
- Pre-registration (committed before the first run): https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor/blob/main/prereg.json
- Changes after the pre-registration, with reasons: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor/blob/main/prereg-log.json
- Cost sources: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/fallfloor/blob/main/sources/costs.json

## Facts

- Machines in the measured run: one laptop (Intel Core i7-1255U, Iris Xe graphics, 16 GB). Each node was a separate Chrome process with its own profile, linked by real WebRTC data channels on that machine. No signalling server, no relay server, no cloud model.
- Models: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (q4f16_1, Apache 2.0) at every station; Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (q4f16_1, Qwen Research licence) as the one-model baseline only.
- Data: Banking77 (CC BY 4.0), SMS Spam Collection v.1 (CC BY 4.0), CLINC150 (CC BY 3.0); 100 held-out items per department.
